purpose: Observed peak fall color, read from the published grading sources, so the predicted windows in predictions.json can be scored. Written before the season starts so the rules are fixed before any observation exists.
recorded_by: The ds-leaf-grading scheduled task reads the sources every Monday and appends entries here. Anything a person adds by hand follows the same schema and is equally welcome.
how_to_record: One entry per reading. Either name a town with `slug`, or, when the source reports by elevation band the way the regional reports do, give `applies_to_elevation_ft` and every tracked town inside that band is scored against it. `observed` is a single ISO date or a {start, end} band. `observed_on` is the day the source was read, which is not the day the color peaked. Every entry carries `source_id`, `source_url`, and an `evidence` paraphrase of what the source actually said, so any call can be audited against the page it came from. An entry may also carry `year` (the season the observation describes) -- scripts/score_leaf.py refuses to join an observation whose `year` disagrees with predictions.json's `target_year`, so a prior season's facts can be kept on record without being scored against the current season's windows.
hard_rules: Never record an observation from a source that publishes a PREDICTION rather than an observation. Grading our forecast against another forecast is not grading. This is why fall-color-highcountryhost carries purpose 'leaf-model benchmark' in the registry and must never appear here.
Never infer an observation from our own prediction, and never record a reading whose source was not actually opened.
An entry with no source_id is not an observation. tests/test_score_leaf.py fails the suite if one appears.

Record what the source said, not what it implies about our score. A source describing 'past peak' constrains the peak from above and is worth recording as such; a source saying 'still green' constrains it from below. Neither is a peak date, and neither should be written down as one. A constraint like this is recorded WITHOUT an `observed` field (use `constraint` instead, see below) -- score_leaf.py then refuses it for the honest reason 'no observed date', which is exactly the ungraded-but-on-the-record outcome this rule requires. Never invent a fake peak date to give a constraint a scoreable `observed`.

When a source is ambiguous about timing but IS naming a peak (not just a constraint), record a {start, end} band rather than inventing a single date. A wide honest band scores worse than a lucky guess, which is correct.

fallcolorguy.org (source_id fall-color-fallcolorguy) is internal-only: owner ruling 2026-09-03 permits ingesting his OBSERVATIONS as structured facts (place, elevation band, date, peak status) because facts are not ownable -- his prose is. His PREDICTIONS never enter this file (log them in planning/analysis/2026-09-03-fall-color-guy-benchmark.md's benchmark log instead). No verbatim prose from him is ever recorded here, only paraphrased `evidence`. The registry's `internal_only: true` flag on his row keeps him off the public /leaf page regardless of what happens in this file (src/lib/leaf.ts:getLeafGradingSources).

confidence_levels.explicit: The source named a peak, or a peak range, in so many words.
confidence_levels.inferred: The source described conditions from which a peak is readable (a 9-of-10 color rating, 'past peak at this elevation'), but did not use the word.
confidence_levels.weak: The reading is a judgment call worth recording with its uncertainty. Scored like any other, and flagged so a person can overrule it.
confidence_levels.constraint: The source bounds a peak from one side ('past peak by X', 'still good through Y') without naming a date. Recorded with a `constraint` object instead of `observed`, and never scored -- score_leaf.py's normal 'no observed date' refusal is the mechanism, not a special case.

cadence.plan: Every Monday from September 21 through November 9, the ds-leaf-grading scheduled task reads each grading source, appends any new peak call here with its evidence, reruns scripts/score_leaf.py, and commits both files together.
cadence.why_not_scraped: All the sources are human-judged prose and photo galleries. No station reports a peak-color number. A scraper would dress a judgment call up as a measurement, so each page is read and the reading is recorded with the evidence behind it.
